Salary Tax Calculator Pakistan 2025-26

This salary tax calculator Pakistan employees can trust uses the Finance Act 2025 slabs for tax year 2025-26. Enter your monthly or annual salary and see the tax, the Section 4AB surcharge where it applies, and your take-home pay.

🔒 Your files never leave your device.

How to use

  1. Enter your gross monthly salary — or your annual salary in the second box.
  2. Press Calculate tax.
  3. Read your annual and monthly tax, any surcharge, and your take-home salary.

How it works

Salaried tax for 2025-26 is slab-based: no tax up to Rs 600,000 a year; 1% on the part between Rs 600,000 and Rs 1,200,000; then fixed amounts plus 11%, 23%, 30% and 35% on the parts in the higher slabs. On top of this, Section 4AB adds a surcharge of 9% of the tax when annual taxable income exceeds Rs 10,000,000 — the calculator shows it as its own line. These are the 2025-26 slabs under the Finance Act 2025; tax is normally withheld monthly by your employer.

Worked example: Example: a monthly salary of Rs 100,000 is Rs 1,200,000 a year. Tax = 1% of the Rs 600,000 above the exempt slab = Rs 6,000 per year, just Rs 500 a month; take-home is Rs 99,500 a month.

Frequently asked questions

What is the tax-free salary limit in Pakistan for 2025-26?

Salaried income up to Rs 600,000 per year (Rs 50,000 per month) is exempt from income tax in tax year 2025-26.

How much tax is deducted on a Rs 100,000 monthly salary?

Rs 100,000 a month is Rs 1,200,000 a year, which gives a tax of Rs 6,000 per year — Rs 500 per month.

What is the Section 4AB surcharge?

When annual taxable income exceeds Rs 10,000,000, an extra surcharge of 9% of the calculated income tax is charged under Section 4AB. This calculator shows it as a separate line.

Are salaried and non-salaried tax slabs the same?

No. Salaried individuals have their own slab table, which is more favourable at lower incomes. This calculator uses the salaried table only.

Is this the final tax I will pay?

It is an accurate estimate on salary alone. Other income, tax credits, deductible allowances and adjustments by your employer or in your annual return can change the final figure.
